tickets.title: Spike: calibrate the Haiku judge against ~30 human labels
tickets.summary: Measure Cohen's kappa between the Haiku 5.5 judge and ~30 human labels and record whether L2 numbers can be trusted.
tickets.description: Spike (must finish before any L2 number is trusted). Build a calibration set of ~30 (question, answer, cited excerpts) items drawn from the existing data/eval/golden_qa.json and a few saved model answers, each with a human label for faithfulness (pass/fail) and citation correctness (pass/fail) stored in data/eval/judge_calibration.json (labels entered by the operator; the ticket supplies the file schema, a labelling CLI `python -m scripts.label_calibration`, and the runner). Run the judge (`LLM_MODEL_JUDGE` = claude-haiku-5-5, must differ from `LLM_MODEL_ANSWER`) with the existing data/eval/judge_prompt.txt as the starting prompt, in both A/B and swapped order where the prompt is pairwise (MT-Bench swap-order check). Compute Cohen's kappa per metric. Write the result to docs/adr/judge-calibration.md with: n, kappa per metric, confusion matrix, prompt version, and a go/no-go statement. Quote ADR-017: "Haiku 5.5 judge ... calibrated on ~30 human labels (Cohen's kappa)"; trigger to revisit: "Judge kappa below acceptable". Out of scope: the Ragas runner (E7-T8), choosing a different judge model (a no-go result is reported, not fixed here).
acceptance_criteria: Given the ~30 labelled items, `python -m scripts.calibrate_judge` prints kappa for faithfulness and citation and exits 0; a unit test with a fixed fake judge and known labels asserts the kappa value equals the hand-computed value (e.g. 0.6) to 3 decimals.
docs/adr/judge-calibration.md exists in the repo and contains n >= 30, a kappa value per metric, the judge model id and the prompt file hash; a CI check (grep test) fails if any of these is missing.
Unit test: the calibration runner raises if LLM_MODEL_JUDGE equals LLM_MODEL_ANSWER.
The ADR states an explicit threshold used for go/no-go and the decision (go or no-go) next to the measured kappa.

tickets.title: Define the golden-set schema and loader with tenant parameters
tickets.summary: Give the golden set a validated, tenant-parameterised schema and migrate the existing 50-or-fewer cases into it.
tickets.description: The repo already has data/eval/golden_qa.json and scripts/run_eval.py (MVP). Define a Pydantic model `GoldenCase` {id, category (answerable, adversarial, refusal, cross_tenant, tier, jurisdiction), question, persona (advisor tier, jurisdictions, licenses, role as a template, never a hard-coded tenant id), tenant_param (placeholder resolved to the `eval` tenant via `EVAL_TENANT_ID` at run time), expected_chunk_ids or expected_doc_refs (for L1), must_cite_refs, must_not_contain, expected_refusal (code or null), reference_answer (optional, for Ragas), notes}. Add a loader `load_golden(path)` that validates every case, rejects duplicate ids and unknown categories, and resolves tenant parameters. Convert the existing cases to the schema (target: 50 cases at this ticket). Quote ADR-017: "Golden set 50 growing to ~300, tenant-parameterised." Out of scope: adding cases beyond 50 (E7-T3), runners.
acceptance_criteria: Given a golden file with a duplicate id, `load_golden` raises ValueError naming the id (unit test).
Given a case with a hard-coded tenant uuid instead of the placeholder, validation fails (unit test).
`pytest backend/tests/test_golden_set.py` passes and asserts the shipped file holds >= 50 cases covering every category name at least once except where E7-T3 adds them.
With EVAL_TENANT_ID set to uuid X, every resolved case reports tenant_id == X (unit test).

tickets.title: Add adversarial, refusal and leak-probe cases to the golden set
tickets.summary: Extend the golden set with adversarial, refusal, and cross-tenant / tier / jurisdiction probe cases.
tickets.description: Add at least 40 cases to the golden set: prompt-injection attempts in the question and in retrieved text, requests the system must refuse (no firm documentation -> NO_FIRM_DOCUMENTATION refusal, out-of-jurisdiction, above-tier content), and cross-tenant probes (a question whose only matching content belongs to another tenant, so the right answer is a refusal and no foreign chunk id may appear). Each case sets expected_refusal or must_not_contain. Add seed fixtures (a second synthetic tenant with distinct content, plus restricted-tier and other-jurisdiction documents inside the `eval` tenant) under data/eval/fixtures/ so that probes have something to leak. Quote ADR-017 L3: "cross-tenant / tier / jurisdiction refusal and promptfoo red team" and OWASP table LLM01/LLM08 tests. Out of scope: the runner that executes them (E7-T10).
acceptance_criteria: `pytest backend/tests/test_golden_set.py` asserts >= 40 cases in categories adversarial, refusal, cross_tenant, tier, jurisdiction, with at least 5 in each.
Test asserts every cross_tenant case names a foreign-tenant chunk id in a `forbidden_chunk_ids` field that exists in the fixtures.
Loading the fixtures into a test database via the existing seed path creates documents for two tenants and the test fails if the second tenant has no chunks.

tickets.title: Grow the golden set to about 300 curated cases
tickets.summary: Reach ~300 golden cases, curated per tenant and balanced by category.
tickets.description: Grow data/eval/golden_qa.json to 280-320 cases across answerable, adversarial and refusal categories, parameterised by tenant (the `eval` tenant plus the second fixture tenant). Cases are authored from the corpus documents (regulatory refs and chunk ids must resolve). Add a coverage script `python -m scripts.golden_stats` that prints counts per category and per document and fails on unresolved expected chunk ids. Quote ADR-017: "Golden set 50 growing to ~300"; consequence: "the golden set must be curated per tenant". Out of scope: the human calibration labels (E7-T1).
acceptance_criteria: `python -m scripts.golden_stats` exits 0 and reports total between 280 and 320.
A test fails if any expected_chunk_id / expected_doc_ref does not exist in the seeded eval-tenant corpus.
A test fails if any category has fewer than 5% of total cases or any single document is referenced by more than 10% of answerable cases.

tickets.title: Build the eval job entrypoint, Langfuse datasets and run record
tickets.summary: Provide a `jobs eval` entrypoint that runs as fa_eval against the eval tenant, syncs the golden set to Langfuse and emits EvalRunCompleted.
tickets.description: Add the `eval` Cloud Run job entrypoint on the existing `jobs` image entrypoint (arch 4.8: `eval` | `fa_eval` | "Full or subset eval run (L1-L3) against the dedicated `eval` tenant; results to Langfuse and `eval.events.v1`"). Arguments: `--subset pr|full`, `--layers l1,l2,l3`, `--model answer|fallback`. It opens DB connections as `fa_eval` only (role created in E1), pinned to `EVAL_TENANT_ID`; it must refuse to start if EVAL_TENANT_ID is unset or if the connected role is not fa_eval. It syncs the golden set to a Langfuse dataset (`run_experiment`), writes a JSON result file (metrics, git sha, model ids, prompt version) and produces `EvalRunCompleted` on `eval.events.v1` with the `eval` service-account Kafka key using an idempotent producer (event_id derived from run id). The ~60-question PR subset is selected by a `subset: pr` flag on cases (stratified, set in this ticket for existing cases). Out of scope: metric computation (T6, T8, T10), CI wiring (T12).
acceptance_criteria: Given DB user fa_app, the entrypoint exits non-zero with a message naming the role mismatch (unit test).
Given EVAL_TENANT_ID unset, the entrypoint exits non-zero before any DB or LLM call (unit test).
`--subset pr` selects between 55 and 65 cases and every category is represented (unit test on the shipped golden set once T3 is merged).
Integration test with the CI Kafka container: a dry run produces exactly one EvalRunCompleted message; running it twice with the same run id yields one logical event (dedupe on event_id).

tickets.title: Implement L1 retrieval metrics: recall@k, MRR and nDCG
tickets.summary: Compute retrieval quality metrics for a retrieval configuration over the golden set.
tickets.description: In `backend/src/evals/l1.py` (or the repo's existing eval package location) compute recall@k (k in 5, 10, 15), MRR and nDCG@10 per case and aggregate, calling the production `RetrievalService.search` path under the `fa_eval` role and the `eval` tenant so RLS applies exactly as in chat. Accept a config object {mode: dense|fts|hybrid|hybrid_rerank, rerank_candidates, contextual_headers: bool}, which sets the corresponding settings for the run only (RRF_K 60, HNSW settings from config). Record p50/p95 latency of the first stage and of rerank per config. Only answerable cases with expected chunk ids are scored. Output JSON per config. Quote ADR-008: "RRF k = 60 in one SQL statement with RLS on both legs" and ADR-017 L1. Out of scope: choosing the winning config (E7-T7).
acceptance_criteria: Unit test with a fake retriever and hand-built ranked lists asserts recall@5, MRR and nDCG@10 equal hand-computed values to 4 decimals.
Integration test (real pgvector in CI) runs mode=dense and mode=hybrid on 5 seeded cases and returns metrics with latency fields non-null.
Test asserts the L1 run opens its connection as fa_eval and that a query using a foreign tenant id returns zero results.

tickets.title: Spike: run the retrieval ablation and decide rerank and contextual retrieval
tickets.summary: Run dense / FTS / hybrid / rerank (with and without contextual headers) ablation and record the decisions.
tickets.description: Spike. Using E7-T6, run these configs over the full golden set: dense, FTS, hybrid (RRF k=60), hybrid + rerank with RERANK_CANDIDATES in {10, 15, 20, 30}, each with CONTEXTUAL_RETRIEVAL_ENABLED on and off (requires the corpus re-indexed with and without `chunks.context_header`). Record recall@5/10/15, MRR, nDCG@10 and first-stage / rerank p95 latency. Write docs/adr/retrieval-ablation.md with the table and these decisions: RERANK_ENABLED (kept or dropped), RERANK_CANDIDATES (value in range 10-30), CONTEXTUAL_RETRIEVAL_ENABLED (kept or dropped). Quote ADR-008: "kept or dropped by the eval ablation on recall and latency; `RERANK_CANDIDATES` default 15 (range 10-30), set by the L1 ablation (D14.1)" and ADR-016: "The L1 ablation decides whether it stays." The ticket also records the latency budget check: first stage p95 < 300 ms, rerank p95 < 700 ms. Out of scope: GATE_MIN_SCORE (set in E3-T16). Applying the chosen values to config defaults is part of this ticket (config change only).
acceptance_criteria: docs/adr/retrieval-ablation.md exists with one row per config containing recall@10, MRR, nDCG@10 and p95 latency as numbers; a grep test fails on empty cells.

The ADR states RERANK_ENABLED, RERANK_CANDIDATES (between 10 and 30) and CONTEXTUAL_RETRIEVAL_ENABLED each as kept/dropped or a value, with the recall delta in points and latency delta in ms that justify it.
The default values in `Settings` equal the ADR decisions (unit test reads both).
Rerun of the winning config reproduces recall@10 within 1 point of the ADR value (command recorded in the ADR).

tickets.title: Implement L2 Ragas runner with CI lower bounds
tickets.summary: Score answers with Ragas collections using the Haiku judge and report metrics with confidence-interval lower bounds.
tickets.description: Implement the L2 runner: for each answerable case run the real chat pipeline (answer model from `--model`) as fa_eval on the eval tenant, then score with Ragas collections API (pinned version): faithfulness, context precision, context recall, noise sensitivity, plus the deterministic citation score from the E4 CitationVerifier output (do not reimplement the verifier; call E4-T11). Judge model is `LLM_MODEL_JUDGE`; the runner refuses to run if judge == answer model. Report each metric as mean plus a bootstrap 95% confidence interval and its lower bound (ARES-style, arXiv 2311.09476). Refuse to emit gate-eligible numbers unless docs/adr/judge-calibration.md records a go decision (read a machine-readable `judge_calibration.json` written by E7-T1 containing kappa and `go`). Out of scope: the gate comparison (T11).
acceptance_criteria: Unit test: bootstrap CI on a fixed score vector with fixed seed returns the hand-verified lower bound to 3 decimals.
Unit test: runner raises when judge model equals answer model.
Unit test: runner raises a clear error when judge_calibration.json is missing or has go=false.
Integration test with a stub LLM and stub judge on 5 cases produces a result JSON with mean, ci_low, ci_high for faithfulness, context_precision, context_recall, noise_sensitivity and citation.

tickets.title: Implement L3 refusal, tier, jurisdiction and cross-tenant runner
tickets.summary: Execute the refusal and leak-probe golden cases and count leaks.
tickets.description: Run all cases in categories refusal, cross_tenant, tier, jurisdiction, adversarial through the real chat API path as fa_eval/eval tenant personas. A leak is defined as: any returned citation, SSE event, or answer text containing a chunk id, document id or marker from `forbidden_chunk_ids`, or an answer where expected_refusal is set but no refusal event occurred. Output {refusal_pass_rate, leaks} and the offending case ids. Quote ADR-017: "Gate: ... leaks = 0" and OWASP LLM02/LLM08 tests. Add a way to plant a leak for self-tests: env flag `EVAL_PLANT_LEAK=1` is NOT allowed in production code; instead the runner accepts an injected `retriever_override` used only by tests. Out of scope: promptfoo red team (T15).
acceptance_criteria: Unit test with a fake chat client that returns a forbidden chunk id: runner reports leaks == 1 and names the case.
Unit test with a fake client that answers instead of refusing on a refusal case: refusal_pass_rate < 1.0.
Integration test (real DB, stub LLM) with the shipped probes: leaks == 0 and the run exits 0 on the unmodified pipeline.
Test asserts no production module reads an EVAL_PLANT_LEAK-style env flag (grep test).

tickets.title: Add the gate evaluator with thresholds and recall baseline
tickets.summary: Compare run results to the gate thresholds and the stored recall baseline and fail with a clear reason.
tickets.description: Implement `python -m scripts.eval_gate result.json --baseline data/eval/baseline.json` that exits non-zero if: citation < 0.95, faithfulness < 0.90 (judged on the CI lower bound when the full run, on the point estimate on the PR subset), leaks > 0, or recall@10 drops by more than 2 points versus baseline. Thresholds are constants in config (not scattered). Add `scripts.eval_baseline_update` to write a new baseline (manual, reviewed in PR). Quote ADR-017: "Gate: citation >= 0.95, faithfulness >= 0.90, leaks = 0, recall regression <= 2 pts" and "gate thresholds need re-tuning when the corpus grows". Output a one-line failure reason per breached rule. Out of scope: running the metrics (T6, T8, T9) and CI wiring (T11).
acceptance_criteria: Parametrised unit tests: citation 0.949 fails, 0.95 passes; faithfulness 0.899 fails, 0.90 passes; leaks 1 fails; recall drop 2.1 points fails, 2.0 passes.
Each failing case prints the rule name and the measured and required values (asserted by output match).
A missing baseline file makes the gate exit non-zero with a message (unit test), never pass silently.

tickets.title: Wire the path-filtered PR eval job in CI
tickets.summary: Run the ~60-question subset as the blocking `eval` job on relevant PRs.
tickets.description: Add a GitHub Actions workflow `eval-pr.yml` extending the E0 CI (Postgres with pgvector and Kafka service containers already exist): path filter on backend/src/{retrieval,agent,guardrails,llm,prompts}, data/eval, and prompt files; steps: migrate, seed the eval tenant, run `jobs eval --subset pr --layers l1,l2,l3` as fa_eval, then `scripts.eval_gate`; upload result JSON as an artifact; fail the check on gate failure. Secrets for Anthropic and Voyage come from GitHub secrets; the job runs only when secrets exist (fork PRs skip with a visible neutral status). Out of scope: the weekly workflow (T13); the L0 jobs (E0/E1).
acceptance_criteria: On a PR touching backend/src/retrieval the workflow runs and the check named `eval` appears; on a docs-only PR it does not run (verified by a workflow path-filter test via `act` or recorded run links in the PR description).
A forced gate failure (E7-T12 fixtures) turns the `eval` check red; the green path posts the metrics table as an artifact.
The job's DB user is fa_eval (assert in a CI step that `select current_user` equals fa_eval).

tickets.title: Prove the gate with four deliberate-regression test PRs
tickets.summary: Show that the PR gate fails for each of four seeded regressions.
tickets.description: Create four regression patches kept as reviewed fixtures under tests/eval_gate/regressions/: (1) break the citation verifier call so citation < 0.95; (2) change the system prompt to encourage unsupported claims so faithfulness < 0.90; (3) plant a cross-tenant leak by dropping the tenant predicate in a retriever double used by the eval run (via the retriever_override from E7-T9, not by editing production RLS); (4) lower RERANK_CANDIDATES / disable the FTS leg so recall@10 drops by more than 2 points. Add a workflow `eval-gate-selftest.yml` (manual dispatch) that applies each patch to a throwaway branch, runs the PR eval job, and asserts the gate fails with the expected rule. Open four draft PRs and record their links and the failing rule in docs/eval/gate-proof.md. Quote the epic done-when: "The PR gate fails a deliberate regression in each of: citation < 0.95, faithfulness < 0.90, a planted cross-tenant leak, recall drop > 2 points (four test PRs)."
acceptance_criteria: For each of the four patches, the selftest workflow reports the eval job failed with the rule name citation, faithfulness, leaks or recall respectively (four recorded run URLs in docs/eval/gate-proof.md).
A fifth control run with no patch passes the gate.
A test fails if docs/eval/gate-proof.md lists fewer than four PR links or any entry lacks the measured value.

tickets.title: Add the weekly full eval run with CI lower bounds
tickets.summary: Run the full golden set weekly and before demos, reporting lower bounds.
tickets.description: Add a scheduled workflow `eval-full.yml` (cron weekly plus workflow_dispatch for before-demo runs) that runs `jobs eval --subset full --layers l1,l2,l3` against the answer model, applies `scripts.eval_gate` using CI lower bounds for faithfulness and citation, publishes a Markdown report (metrics, CI low/high, per-category breakdown, comparison with baseline) to the workflow summary and to Langfuse, and emits EvalRunCompleted. Quote ADR-017: "the full set runs weekly and before demos". Cloud Scheduler/Cloud Run job scheduling is E10; this ticket is the CI/GitHub-hosted run only.
acceptance_criteria: After a workflow_dispatch run the summary contains ci_low for faithfulness and citation as numbers; a test on the report generator fails if any is missing.
The run uses the full set (>= 280 cases) asserted by the result JSON `n_cases`.
A forced faithfulness lower bound below 0.90 in a stub run makes the job fail (unit test on the report/gate step).

tickets.title: Run the full eval against the fallback model and gate LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED
tickets.summary: Evaluate claude-sonnet-4-6 once and make enabling the fallback depend on that result.
tickets.description: Run `jobs eval --subset full --model fallback` using LLM_MODEL_FALLBACK (claude-sonnet-4-6) and store the result as data/eval/fallback_result.json with the gate verdict. Add a startup check in config validation: `LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED=true` is rejected unless data/eval/fallback_result.json (or the configured eval-record location) shows pass for the same fallback model id and a prompt version equal to current PROMPT_VERSION. Quote config table: "`LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED` ... `false` until the gate passes against it" and ADR-017: "once against the fallback model".
acceptance_criteria: Unit test: Settings with LLM_FALLBACK_ENABLED=true and no passing record raises at boot.
Unit test: a passing record for a different model id or different PROMPT_VERSION still raises.
A fallback full-run result exists in the repo with model id claude-sonnet-4-6 and the gate verdict recorded as pass or fail with numbers.

tickets.title: Add the promptfoo red-team job
tickets.summary: Run a promptfoo red team against the API as fa_eval in the redteam job.
tickets.description: Add a promptfoo config (pinned version) under evals/redteam/ targeting the chat API in an ephemeral environment, with plugins for prompt injection, system prompt leakage, PII, cross-tenant/BOLA-style probes and excessive agency, mapped to OWASP LLM01, LLM02, LLM06, LLM07 (arch 8.1 tests column). Add the `redteam` job entrypoint (DB role `fa_eval`, eval tenant) and a CI workflow step on the weekly workflow; a failing probe category fails the job. Out of scope: golden-set L3 (T9).
acceptance_criteria: `promptfoo redteam run` in CI against the stub-LLM stack produces a report artifact and exits non-zero when a seeded vulnerable prompt (test fixture) leaks the system prompt.
Config test asserts plugins cover LLM01, LLM02, LLM06, LLM07 (named mapping in the file).
The redteam job fails to start if the connected DB role is not fa_eval (unit test).

tickets.title: Emit eval.sample.v1 outbox rows and thumbs feedback events
tickets.summary: Have chat-api sample EVAL_SAMPLE_RATE of completed turns into the outbox and send feedback to eval.events.v1.
tickets.description: In chat-api's end-of-turn transaction (arch flow 1: "persist assistant message, turn_events, outbox rows (chat.audit, chat.usage, sampled eval.sample)") add the sampled `TurnSampled` outbox row {message_id, redacted question, redacted answer, cited excerpts (redacted)} for a fraction `EVAL_SAMPLE_RATE` (default 0.05, allowed 0.05-0.10, validated). Sampling is deterministic from message_id hash so tests are repeatable. Ensure `POST /v1/messages/{id}/feedback` (`{score: -1|1, comment?}`) writes `feedback` and an outbox `FeedbackRecorded` for `eval.events.v1`. Only redacted text enters the payload. Do this only if E4/E6 have not already implemented the pieces: check the repo and implement the missing parts. Out of scope: the relay (E5).
acceptance_criteria: Unit test: with EVAL_SAMPLE_RATE=0.10 over 1000 synthetic message ids between 8% and 12% are sampled; with 0 none; the setting rejects 0.5.
Integration test: a completed turn selected by the sampler leaves one outbox row of type TurnSampled whose payload contains no raw PII fixture value.
Integration test: POST feedback with score 1 creates a feedback row and a FeedbackRecorded outbox row; score 2 returns 422.

tickets.title: Implement the eval-judge worker role
tickets.summary: Consume eval.sample.v1, judge with Haiku 5.5 and write Langfuse scores and eval_scores.
tickets.description: Add worker role `eval-judge` (selected via WORKER_ROLES) on the E5 Kafka consumer framework, group `cg.eval-judge`. For each `TurnSampled`: envelope check (tenant_id equals key and not PUBLIC, else dlq.v1), dedupe on message_id + metric via `processed_events`, score faithfulness and citation with `LLM_MODEL_JUDGE` (claude-haiku-5-5, must differ from the answer model) using the calibrated prompt from E7-T1, in one transaction with `app.tenant_id` set insert rows into `eval_scores` {message_id, judge_model, metric, score, rationale (redacted), created_at} as `fa_worker`, send scores to Langfuse (no Langfuse-side evaluators), and write a `JudgeScored` outbox row for `eval.events.v1`. Quote 4.7: "scores the redacted question / answer / cited excerpts with `claude-haiku-5-5` ..., writes scores to Langfuse and `eval_scores`, emits `JudgeScored` on `eval.events.v1`." Out of scope: the sampler (T16), the table and grants (E1).
acceptance_criteria: Unit test: a message whose envelope tenant_id differs from the key goes to dlq.v1 with a reason and writes no score.
Unit test: delivering the same message twice yields one eval_scores row per metric.
Unit test: worker raises at boot if the judge model equals the answer model.
Integration test (CI Postgres + Kafka, stub judge): a TurnSampled message produces rows in eval_scores for the right tenant and an outbox JudgeScored row.

tickets.title: Verify eval-judge end to end with RLS on eval_scores
tickets.summary: Show one sampled turn scored into Langfuse and eval_scores with tenant isolation and no fa_app access.
tickets.description: Add an end-to-end test and a short runbook docs/eval/online-judge.md: chat turn on the eval tenant sampled at rate 1.0 in test -> outbox -> relay -> eval.sample.v1 -> eval-judge -> row in eval_scores and a Langfuse score (Langfuse local container or recorded API call in CI). Also assert the DB-level properties: tenant B's session cannot read tenant A's eval_scores rows; `fa_app` has no privilege on the table. Set the shipped default `EVAL_SAMPLE_RATE` (0.05-0.10) in the demo profile and note the value in the runbook. Quote the done-when: "The `eval-judge` scores at least one sampled turn end to end into Langfuse and `eval_scores` (tenant RLS applies; `fa_app` has no access to the table)."
acceptance_criteria: E2E test passes: after one sampled turn, `select count(*) from eval_scores where message_id = :id` returns >= 2 (faithfulness and citation) and the Langfuse score exists for the trace.
Test: as fa_app, `select * from eval_scores` fails with permission denied.
Test: with app.tenant_id set to tenant B, selecting tenant A's eval_scores rows returns 0 rows.
A feedback POST in the same test run results in a FeedbackRecorded message on eval.events.v1.

questions: Arch does not say who implements the chat-api eval.sample.v1 outbox row and the feedback endpoint (E4, E6 or E7); E7-T16 implements only what is missing. Please confirm the owner.
Arch gives no numeric kappa threshold for 'acceptable' judge agreement (ADR-017 trigger says only 'kappa below acceptable'); E7-T1 records the threshold it chose in the ADR, but a decision is needed.

The PR gate applies faithfulness >= 0.90 and citation >= 0.95; arch does not say whether the PR subset (~60 cases) uses the point estimate or the CI lower bound. E7-T10 uses point estimate on PR and lower bound on the full run.
Arch does not say where the baseline recall file and the fallback-model eval record are stored (repo vs Langfuse vs GCS); tickets store them in the repo under data/eval/.
Arch does not say which source supplies the ~30 human labels (who labels); E7-T1 assumes the operator labels them with a CLI.
The eval job schedule in Cloud Scheduler is not specified for E7; weekly run is implemented as a GitHub Actions cron. Confirm that Cloud Scheduler wiring belongs to E10.
